notDeletedButFixed: The 16-20 February 2026 round-up is deliberately NOT on this list, and it is the useful precedent. On 30/07/2026 the daily curation run opened that index page, found the one relevant notice on it, and rewrote the entry as 'Convatec EsteemBody one-piece intestinal ostomy bag, open-ended (MHRA ref 38578479)' with a real sales angle, autoDetected:false, and a description that says plainly it came off the FSN listing. That is what a round-up is for: a person extracts the notice, automation never guesses it. So a round-up in the feed has two honest endings - curated into a specific notice, or suppressed - and suppression is not automatically the right one. The 6-10 April page below is suppressed because Lou judged it out of scope on 29/07; if it is worth the Convatec treatment instead, delete its entry here and let curation have it.
note: Notices judged NOT to belong in the Compare feed. Read by fetch_issues.py, which never adds a suppressed URL and removes one already stored. This exists because the store is append-only AND the fetcher re-reads still-live sources daily, so deleting a false positive by hand buys one day: on 29/07/2026 three were deleted at 10:33-10:44 BST and the 30/07 07:00 run put them straight back, stamped as new. A judgement has to live where the fetcher reads it. Keyed on source URL, which is stable. Suppressing a notice says nothing about whether the notice is TRUE - the Philips one below is accurate and about real ventilators. It says the notice is not about this audience's specialities. An item carrying a human 'use' line is never removed by this list; it is logged and left for a person.

https://www.gov.uk/drug-device-alerts/fi.reason: gov.uk weekly round-up INDEX page, not a notice. Names no single product and never says what any fault was. Reached the feed under continence on a word buried in the page body. Round-ups are now refused outright by fetch_issues.py; this entry clears the one already stored.

https://www.supplychain.nhs.uk/icn/field.reason: Accurate NHS Supply Chain notice about real Philips ventilators, but respiratory - outside vascular access, continence and urology, and skin prep. Filed here by the product matcher, not by a fault in the notice. Suppressed on scope, not on truth.

https://www.supplychain.nhs.uk/icn/suppl.reason: Record claimed to be 'iCare Medical Ltd nasal cannula with CO2 monitoring FDD3313', flagged SUSPECTED FALSE POSITIVE from 11/08/2026 and re-confirmed daily for 9 consecutive days. Investigated 21/08/2026: FDD3313 is a real NHS Supply Chain product code, but it belongs to Flexicare Medical Ltd (brand 'Dual', Nasal Cannula with CO2 Monitoring) - not iCare Medical. The live page at this URL is ICN 3112, genuinely titled 'Supply Issues Flexicare Medical Ltd Respiratory Solutions and Airway Management Products FDD167 and FAG1727', last updated 19/08/2026 - a real, accurate Flexicare notice. Searched specifically for 'iCare Medical Ltd' as an NHS Supply Chain supplier and found no evidence it exists as a supplier at all. This is not a case of a stable product's URL being retired/reused - the record's premise (an iCare Medical nasal-cannula CO2-monitoring notice) appears to be an auto-detector mis-attribution with no genuine notice to curate into. Two honest endings applied: no real notice exists to re-source to, so suppressed rather than curated.
